nodes.norm_label: when to full restore instead of digest rollback

nodes.label: AsyncAPI Contract
nodes.rationale: Internal channels must never be exposed to tenants/connectors/MCP clients (ADR 0010/0012); public change delivery is gateway-owned only.

nodes.label: OpenAPI Contract
nodes.rationale: Forbids arbitrary SQL, caller-defined vector predicates, raw authorization tuple admin, unrestricted URL fetching, filesystem access, or generic HTTP proxy by contract.

nodes.label: Compatibility Matrix
nodes.rationale: Portable surfaces (REST, MCP, ContextPacket, conformance, skills, AuthZ model) version independently so a skills pack bump does not falsely imply an API bump.

nodes.label: Bounded Adaptive Retrieval Routing (ADR 0015)
nodes.rationale: Planning stays in the agent harness, not an LLM inside Context Fabric, so the server can AuthZ-gate every tool call and enforce absolute retrieval caps rather than trusting model-driven planning.

nodes.label: Skill: access-request
nodes.rationale: Filing an access request instead of retrying an unauthorized fetch prevents escalation loops; skills explicitly cannot approve requests themselves.

nodes.label: Skill: brief-assembly
nodes.rationale: Prefer brief over search when resource_ids are already known, per ADR 0015 step 1, to avoid unnecessary search overhead.

nodes.label: Skill: connect-auth
nodes.rationale: Short-lived bearer tokens and resource metadata verification prevent secret leakage and ensure tokens are scoped to the correct MCP resource.

nodes.label: Skill: governed-recall
nodes.rationale: Sparse-first recall (ADR 0015) routes by known-ness of resource_id/seed to minimize unnecessary broad search and respects server-side caps rather than inventing pagination.

nodes.label: Skill: graph-investigation
nodes.rationale: Bounded depth traversal (default depth 1, optional depth 2) avoids unbounded graph exploration and relies on AuthZ-filtered endpoints rather than client-side visibility assumptions.

nodes.label: Context Fabric Skill Packs (non-authoritative)
nodes.rationale: Skills teach orchestration only and are explicitly kept out of the authorization boundary so prompt injection or skill misuse cannot widen access.

nodes.label: TypeScript client README
nodes.rationale: Recommends audience-bound tokens and OAuth protected-resource metadata instead of embedding secrets in the SDK.

nodes.label: ADR 0010: Change Feed and Webhook Exposure
nodes.norm_label: adr 0010: change feed and webhook exposure
nodes.rationale: Public change delivery is gateway-owned only (cursor feed + signed webhooks) because exposing internal NATS derived streams would invite shadow context stores; events carry only opaque IDs/state/versions/cursor, never content or authorization tuples, so consumers must hydrate via authorized search/get/brief.

nodes.label: ADR 0013: Knowledge-Graph-First
nodes.rationale: Organizational context is inherently relational, but knowledge edges must never become the ACL system; access profile stays derived from OpenFGA ReBAC + policy obligations, with traversal AuthZ-first then policy-final so denied/placeholder neighbors never leak.

nodes.label: ADR 0014: Durable AuthZ Tuple Synchronization
nodes.rationale: Writing OpenFGA tuples after the ledger commit created split-brain risk (intake could succeed while AuthZ sync failed with no re-sync on replay), so a transactional outbox pattern guarantees parent-edge AuthZ tuples are enqueued in the same transaction as the ledger write.

nodes.label: Backup and Restore
nodes.rationale: Restores must replay tombstones/revocations before opening serve ready so a restored system never re-exposes deleted resources; OpenFGA tuples restored after ledger edges with outbox reconciliation to converge sync_authz parents.

nodes.label: Degraded Mode
nodes.rationale: Context Fabric prefers to fail closed on disclosure rather than serve stale governed context when dependencies fail, e.g. denying retrieval rather than falling back to open filters when AuthZ is unavailable.

nodes.label: Release Gates (CI)
nodes.rationale: CI gates map to the stress-test/stress-ratify program so a release candidate must prove authz matrix, replay, tombstone, MCP parity, graph AuthZ, AuthZ outbox, export, webhook metadata-only, and tag non-widening behavior before shipping.

nodes.label: Retrieval Evaluation Corpus (FTS + graph gate)
nodes.rationale: Dense fusion is only enabled if held-out evaluation shows statistically credible material Recall@K/nDCG gains over FTS+graph within latency/cost SLOs, and only opted-in, hash-deduplicated summaries are embedded, never raw evidence by default.

nodes.label: Capacity SLO Baselines
nodes.rationale: SLO numbers are kept as TBD placeholders instead of guessed from architecture diagrams because they must be measurement-derived from a 72h staging soak under representative tenant mix and load.

nodes.label: Helm values.yaml (scaled profile)
nodes.rationale: Scaled profile defaults to external dependencies; bundled connectionMode opt-in only.

nodes.label: Upgrade Order
nodes.rationale: Strict component upgrade ordering (drain, migrate, authz model, serve, workers, verify) exists so authz and ledger stay consistent; workers must never run ahead of migrations.

nodes.label: Plugin Authoring Guide
nodes.rationale: Connectors are restricted to public APIs, default-deny egress, and cannot broaden ACLs or ceilings, to contain blast radius if a connector is compromised.

nodes.label: Context Fabric Threat Model (STRIDE)
nodes.rationale: Trust boundaries and STRIDE mitigations are documented so components fail closed (e.g. tag downgrade must not grant access, agent must not retain creator rights after role revoke).

nodes.label: Chatwoot MappingSpec (map_chatwoot_messages)
nodes.rationale: Constraints (cannot_mint_organization, cannot_broaden_acl, authority_ceiling_from_source, client_fields_may_only_narrow) enforce that connector-mapped fields cannot escalate trust or visibility beyond source authority.

nodes.label: Skill: decision-diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Diagnosis must use authoritative REST endpoints rather than skill inference, to avoid disclosing denied fields or bypassing authorization.

nodes.label: OpenFGA Sample Tuples
nodes.rationale: Fixtures only; customer-facing REST/MCP authentication is out of v1 (ADR 0012).

nodes.label: Starter/Demo Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: Only serve publishes a host port; all dependencies stay private.

nodes.label: Demo Deployment Profile
nodes.rationale: Non-production one-command demo with fully bundled dependencies and synthetic OIDC; fails closed on dependency failures.

nodes.label: Scaled Deployment Profile
nodes.rationale: Kubernetes scaled profile with independently scalable roles and fully external managed dependencies.

nodes.label: Starter Deployment Profile
nodes.rationale: Homelab/starter profile with bundled infra and separate serve, worker, and connector roles.

nodes.label: XSAMA Deployment Profile
nodes.rationale: XSAMA Coolify reference profile — private DB/NATS/S3/OpenFGA LXCs, public serve only, external OIDC (Logto via generic adapter).

nodes.label: Context Fabric Historical Reference Architecture
nodes.rationale: Historical design reference kept for background/rationale; active decisions live in ADRs which win on conflict.

nodes.label: XSAMA Coolify Deployment Notes
nodes.rationale: Dependencies are external on dedicated private LXCs; only serve is public.

nodes.label: ADR 0001: One-Image Role Topology
nodes.rationale: Five separate deployable services made Compose/Coolify/Helm installs hard and risked splitting retrieval from authorization; a single signed multi-arch image with role subcommands avoids second-data-plane risk and simplifies SBOM/release cadence.

nodes.label: ADR 0002: Deployment Profiles
nodes.rationale: Organizations need demo, homelab, XSAMA, and Kubernetes install paths without forking authorization or canonical semantics; profiles vary only packaging (roles, bundled/external deps, public surface).

nodes.label: ADR 0003: Bundled vs External Infra
nodes.rationale: Bundling everything would force forks for orgs with managed RDS/OpenFGA; exposing bundled|external connection modes per dependency lets deployers use existing infra while doctor preflight enforces a minimum capability matrix so gaps fail closed rather than silently non-compliant.

nodes.label: ADR 0004: Generic Intake and MappingSpec
nodes.rationale: Making Chatwoot a special path prevents other platforms from integrating; a generic CloudEvents intake and versioned MappingSpec allow any source to contribute context without minting orgs, broadening ACLs, or exceeding source authority.

nodes.label: ADR 0005: Generated Observations vs Agent Actions
nodes.norm_label: adr 0005: generated observations vs agent actions
nodes.rationale: Organizations need a safe memory-write primitive without granting agents arbitrary mutation or send powers; separating context contribution from agent action prevents prompt injection from escalating into irreversible external actions in v1.

nodes.label: ADR 0006: OpenFGA Policy Ownership and Consistency
nodes.norm_label: adr 0006: openfga policy ownership and consistency
nodes.rationale: OpenFGA, OPA, and Cedar had overlapping concerns and the reference doc overclaimed at_least_as_fresh consistency that OpenFGA cannot provide; standardizing on OpenFGA alone with mapped consistency levels keeps revocation SLOs honest and avoids duplicated allow/deny logic.

nodes.label: ADR 0007: NATS Outbox and Recovery Authority
nodes.norm_label: adr 0007: nats outbox and recovery authority
nodes.rationale: JetStream is only at-least-once, so claiming end-to-end exactly-once across Postgres, S3, parsers, and indexes would be false; making the Postgres transactional outbox the authoritative event source gives a clear recovery authority and RPO story without a public second data plane.

nodes.label: ADR 0008: Tenant and Brand Model
nodes.rationale: Prior docs mixed tenant_id, logto_org_id, and brand_id; canonicalizing on organization_id with brand as an optional governed child scope prevents display tags from being mistaken for tenancy or visibility grants.

nodes.label: ADR 0009: Action Naming Conventions
nodes.rationale: OAuth scopes, delegation actions, MCP tools, and REST paths used inconsistent separators; standardizing context:* scopes vs context.* internal actions keeps a single ApplicationService backing both REST and MCP with OpenFGA still owning resource visibility.

nodes.label: ADR 0011: Connector Trust Tiers
nodes.rationale: Full OCI isolation is correct for untrusted plugins but too heavy for a single first-party Chatwoot connector on day one, so a tiered trust model (Core/Tier0/Tier1/Deterministic transform) is used, with Chatwoot v1 restricted to a separately authenticated connector role with no direct DB/NATS/OpenFGA credentials.

nodes.label: ADR 0012: V1 Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Scope creep (attachments, customer callers, agent send, Kafka, OPA) threatens delivery of a portable governed context plane, so v1 boundaries explicitly exclude these to keep an honest 'v1 complete' definition tied to onboarding, portability, and security gates.

nodes.label: ADR 0015: Sparse-First Retrieval and Portable MCP
nodes.norm_label: adr 0015: sparse-first retrieval and portable mcp
nodes.rationale: Industry evidence shows always-on dense retrieval and always-on deep graph traversal waste cost on easy queries while still missing precise identifiers, so retrieval defaults to sparse FTS + shallow graph, with dense embeddings gated behind held-out evaluation showing material Recall@K/nDCG gains within latency/cost SLOs.

nodes.label: Context Fabric README
nodes.rationale: One signed multi-architecture Go image; packaging profiles do not fork authorization or canonical semantics.
